newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps strengthen, CFDs rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps strengthen, CFDs rise sharply.

text.p: European oil swaps tracked higher on Thursday although activity was fairly slow.

Brent crude CFDs gained up to nine cents and had more of a roller-coaster ride than other instruments, showing sharp morning gains which were partly eased for further out contracts as the day progressed.
News that BP was cutting runs at its Nerefco refinery by the equivalent of 40 pct for the balance of May gave a supportive undertone.

Levels for May 27-30 CFDs firmed to 2.5 cents under July Brent compared with 10 cents on Wednesday and two early morning May 27-30 deals were concluded -7 cents under July. A further May 27-30 was done at July flat.
A June 2-6 CFD was done at 16 cents under July and the market was pegged towards the tail end of the day around this level compared with -15 cents on Wednesday.
Heavy fuel picked up a touch with deals trading on June at $84 at least twice and Q1 going once at $97. Traders said Q4 was holding steady at $94.25.
Physical barges were about $1-2 adrift of these levels with $82 fob ARA done and offer levels even as low as $81.50 although nothing was thought concluded at this level.
Some traders said the physical market was being pressured lower in a pricing move and that any drop in the swaps numbers would generate increased swaps buying.
A low sulphur swap was understood done at $97, although some dealers thought this a touch high.
"I've been seeing it pretty much in a $96.25-$96.75 range all day," said one.

Naphtha was also stronger with June hovering around $192-193, about $2 higher, with July contangoed by up to $1 and August $1 above this. A good quality Immingham cargo was sold at high cif quotes +$2.75-3.
Gasoline was about 50 cents to $1 higher with June around $210 and July backwardated by $5-5.50. A Eurograde barge was done at $210 in the morning while a regular parcel went at $201.50.
